inspection_summary: All 905 logical lines were inspected. The paper builds a cross-domain bridge rather than an argument about the Riemann Hypothesis: fluctuation identities for a Gaussian random walk reduce the expected first ladder height to exponential Dirichlet-type series; analytic continuation and the zeta functional equation then make zeta values explicit Taylor coefficients, locate branch singularities, and accelerate computation, after which the expansion is transported back to overshoots and boundary-crossing probabilities. The PDF extraction preserves prose and high-level transformations but replaces much mathematical punctuation with control-like glyphs, degrades Γ as $, flattens set delimiters and decimals, and disrupts contour integrals, binomial coefficients, fractions, and exponents. Exact symbolic or numerical reuse therefore requires checking the raw PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Summarizes analytic continuation of the expected ladder height, zeta-valued Taylor coefficients, singularities, and probabilistic applications.

sections_inspected.label: Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the Gaussian ladder problem, states the main expansion, motivates the Hardy reparametrization, and identifies the zeta special value with a limiting overshoot coefficient.

sections_inspected.label: Local analytic continuation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transforms a fluctuation identity into an exponential power series, proves its continuation near zero by contour methods and continuation in a parameter, and derives the zeta-coefficient expansion and radius.

sections_inspected.label: Global continuation and singularities
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Subtracts successive branch contributions to enlarge continuation disks, characterizes the periodic singularity pattern, transfers it to the drift variable, and obtains a faster computational series.

sections_inspected.label: Boundary-crossing applications
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses likelihood-ratio and renewal identities to convert the ladder-height expansion into boundary-crossing asymptotics, moments, and derivatives of expected overshoot.

sections_inspected.label: Concluding remarks
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tests and rejects natural probabilistic interpretations of the analytic continuation at negative drift.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgments, references, and affiliations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-mathematical end matter and bibliographic provenance.

accepted_units.title: A drift-parameterized ladder height becomes an analytic object
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines the first ladder epoch and height, recalls zeta continuation, and reframes the small-drift behavior of an expectation as analytic continuation and coefficient extraction around the origin.
accepted_units.context_note: The probabilistic definitions and analytic objective must remain together because the semantic move is the change of representation, not either definition alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Set delimiters, parentheses, and the defining zeta series are glyph-degraded; the prose-level definitions are reliable, while exact notation requires the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Zeta values encode every coefficient of the ladder-height expansion
accepted_units.why_material: The main theorem expresses the full Taylor series using ζ(1/2−n), identifies its convergence disk and branch points, and explains why a reparametrized Hardy series converts slow convergence near zero drift into a rapidly convergent expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem, singularity statement, original slowly convergent series, and Hardy reparametrization form one strategic unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed exponential expansion, disk radius, and branch-point coordinates are line-broken and symbol-degraded; check the raw PDF for exact factors and powers.

accepted_units.title: The coefficient ζ(1/2) is the limiting expected overshoot correction
accepted_units.why_material: Prior small-drift expansions, renewal theory, sequential boundary corrections, and Wiener–Hopf analysis are reconciled by identifying the same constant as both a ladder-height coefficient and −ζ(1/2)/√(2π).
accepted_units.context_note: The historical comparison is retained because it demonstrates that several independently motivated quantities are one structural invariant rather than a numerical coincidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several moments, decimals, and square-root factors are corrupted by extraction; the identification is explicit in prose, but exact numerical values and formulas need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: A fluctuation identity converts ladder heights into an exponential Dirichlet series
accepted_units.why_material: Wald's equation and the fluctuation formula express the expected ladder height through sign probabilities; differentiation and Gaussianity then reduce the problem to a series n^(−α)e^(−nw) near w=0.
accepted_units.context_note: The standard identity, differentiation step, and parameter substitution are kept together to expose the full bridge from probability to complex analysis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The summations and derivative formula have degraded delimiters and roots; the transformation is prose-supported, but exact normalization constants require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Subtracting the principal singular term exposes a zeta-coefficient Taylor series
accepted_units.why_material: A parameterized series is regularized by subtracting its leading singular term; the resulting function continues to a disk around zero and has coefficients c(α)ζ(α−n), from which the ladder-height theorem follows by specialization, integration, and exponentiation.
accepted_units.context_note: The notation, theorem, removable-singularity convention, and deduction of the main result are one reusable regularization pattern.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Γ is extracted as $, multiple fractions are flattened, and the displayed series has ordering defects; the regularization and coefficient claim are clear, but exact formulas require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A contour integral supplies the continuation across the boundary of the original half-plane
accepted_units.why_material: After fixing a logarithm branch, the authors construct matching contours, show the integral representation is analytic on a larger domain, and equate it with the original series by residue calculus and controlled contour limits.
accepted_units.context_note: Branch choice, contour geometry, uniform convergence, Gamma integral, residue term, and final identity are inseparable parts of the continuation mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Figures 1-2 are not textually represented beyond captions, and contour integrals, inequalities, and orientations are heavily flattened. The proof strategy is recoverable, but exact contours and signs must be checked in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Analyticity in a second parameter extends identities beyond their initial convergence range
accepted_units.why_material: The source treats both the series and contour integral as entire functions of α, uses uniform convergence to exchange sums, integrals, and derivatives, and thereby prepares identities proved in a safe half-plane for continuation to all α.
accepted_units.context_note: The conceptual move is two-variable continuation supported by uniform bounds; the derivative formula is retained only as its certificate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Binomial coefficients, derivative notation, and integral denominators are visually degraded, so exact derivative identities need the PDF; the uniform-convergence reasoning is readable.

accepted_units.title: Boundary limits recover zeta coefficients and the functional equation fixes the convergence radius
accepted_units.why_material: Equality of the continued functions transfers derivatives to the boundary, where they are first evaluated in an absolutely convergent range and then extended in α; the zeta functional equation gives coefficient asymptotics and hence the exact radius of the Taylor series.
accepted_units.context_note: Derivative recovery, continuation in α, removable singularities, and the functional-equation asymptotic form a single completion of the local theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Derivative expressions, Gamma factors, cosine terms, and coefficient asymptotics are line-broken; exact calculations require the raw PDF.

accepted_units.title: Removing neighboring branch terms enlarges the continuation disk in controlled stages
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2.4 subtracts a finite family of explicit branch contributions and replaces zeta coefficients by tails, producing a power series whose radius grows with the number of removed singularities.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem and proof are kept together because the altered coefficients, binomial rearrangement, and radius estimate jointly explain why subtraction extends the domain.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Large nested sums, generalized binomial coefficients, branch powers, and the tail notation are severely flattened. The staged-subtraction mechanism is clear, but exact identities must be verified from the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Periodic branch geometry transfers to drift singularities and faster evaluation
accepted_units.why_material: The continued series has periodically repeated branch points with explicit local singular parts; mapping w back to the drift variable locates the ladder-height singularities, while increasing the subtraction depth accelerates convergence on any fixed disk.
accepted_units.context_note: The global singularity summary and computational consequence are grouped because both arise from the same explicit removal of local branch terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Unions of rays, branch powers, and mapped point coordinates are extraction-sensitive; verify their exact orientation and constants in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Likelihood ratios transport the zeta expansion to boundary-crossing probabilities
accepted_units.why_material: A change-of-drift likelihood identity factors the crossing probability into a leading exponential and an overshoot transform; renewal convergence and duality express that transform through the ladder-height expectation, so its zeta-valued Taylor series becomes a crossing-probability expansion.
accepted_units.context_note: The corollary, likelihood identity, limiting overshoot law, exponential error control, duality, and final substitution are one causal chain.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Probability-event braces, exponentials, and the final series are glyph- and layout-degraded; the logical reduction is readable, while exact constants require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: One analytic expansion yields wider asymptotic regimes, moments, and overshoot derivatives
accepted_units.why_material: The source explains when the exponentially small boundary error is dominated by arbitrary drift powers, derives a Poincaré expansion beyond diffusion scaling, and extracts higher ladder-height moments and derivatives of expected overshoot from the same zeta coefficients.
accepted_units.context_note: These consequences are grouped to show reuse of a single coefficient engine rather than treated as unrelated computations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moment superscripts, zeta powers, square roots, decimals, and big-O exponents are degraded; exact formulas and numerical values require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Analytic continuation need not preserve an obvious probabilistic meaning
accepted_units.why_material: For negative drift, two natural conditional expectations are tested and rejected as interpretations of the continued function; Wiener–Hopf factorization instead locates the continuation strictly between them.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a useful obstruction to conflating an analytic continuation with a continuation of the original semantic object.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Conditional-event notation and the factorization formula are glyph-degraded, but the rejected candidates and inequality conclusion are explicit in prose.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A probabilistic observable becomes a zeta-coefficient engine
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A fluctuation identity changes an expectation into an exponential Dirichlet series; subtracting its singular part and continuing analytically turns zeta values into the reusable coefficients of the original probabilistic observable.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The mechanism concerns the Riemann zeta function but supplies no evidence about the Riemann Hypothesis, and exact formulas are extraction-sensitive.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Singularity subtraction is both continuation and acceleration
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Explicitly isolating local branch contributions allows the same representation to cross successive analytic barriers and simultaneously improves numerical convergence on fixed compact regions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Contour geometry depends on missing figures and degraded notation, so this synthesis is secure at the strategic level but not as an exact symbolic derivation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zeta special values coordinate multiple probabilistic quantities
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same zeta-valued expansion controls ladder heights, limiting overshoots, boundary-crossing probabilities, higher moments, and correction terms, revealing that these outputs are projections of one analytic structure.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Several probabilistic limit theorems are cited rather than reproved, and the numerical constants must be checked against the raw source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic extension can sever original semantics
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Continuing a parameterized expectation beyond its original domain preserves analytic identities but need not preserve any obvious conditional-expectation interpretation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The paper rejects two natural candidates but does not supply a positive probabilistic interpretation for negative drift.
